OP

Brazil has just wired a public blockchain into the official plumbing of a top-10 world economy. CSD BR, authorized by the Central Bank, the CVM and SUSEP to register, hold and settle securities, now mirrors live ownership records onto the XRP Ledger. The depository sits on more than BRL 22 trillion in registered assets, roughly $4 trillion, and can clear millions of transactions in minutes. No other public chain is in the stack.

The first assets are investment-fund shares from BTG Pactual, Latin America’s largest investment bank, which runs about R$2.7 trillion in combined wealth and asset management. Those shares are tokenized as Multi-Purpose Tokens on XRPL and paired with Ripple custody. CSD BR stays the legal source of truth for registration, deposit and settlement. XRPL becomes a permissioned, near-real-time audit layer that authorized banks can check under existing KYC and AML rules; no new licenses, no change in investor process, and with freeze and clawback still under CSD BR control.
That is the first time a licensed central securities depository has recorded securities ownership on a public blockchain in live market conditions. Once the mirror holds, the plan is native issuance and trading among approved participants, starting with CRI and CRA; the real-estate and agribusiness receivables that now form more than R$600 billion of Brazil’s private fixed-income stock after a fivefold surge in securitization over a decade.

On September 24, UK Finance announced the successful completion of the first live customer transactions using tokenized sterling deposits through the Great British Tokenized Deposit initiative.

Seven banks are involved:

Barclays, HSBC UK, Lloyds Banking Group, Monzo, Nationwide, NatWest and Santander.

The first live transactions included two remortgage completions and a consumer marketplace transaction.

And UK Finance explicitly states:

The platform was built by Quant.

That’s no longer a PowerPoint.

Real customers. Real bank deposits. Real transactions.

Then look at what Quant was selected to do.

The Clearing House selected Quant to power the interoperability, orchestration and transaction management layer of its On Chain Money Initiative.

That layer will coordinate the clearing and settlement of tokenized deposits while connecting to existing fiat payment infrastructure, including RTP and CHIPS.

And The Clearing House isn’t some crypto startup.

Its U.S. payment networks clear and settle more than $2 trillion every day across wire, ACH, check image and real time payments.

Quant isn’t being brought in to design the website.

It’s being brought in for the infrastructure.

Fair.

Project Rosalind is the perfect example.

In 2023, BIS explicitly described Rosalind as “purely experimental” and said it did not reflect Bank of England intentions regarding CBDC policy, design or launch.

Compare that with 2026.

Quant built the platform behind live UK tokenized deposit transactions.
Murex is integrating Quant’s programmable money infrastructure into MX.3.

The Clearing House selected Quant for its On Chain Money Initiative.
The progression matters:

Experiment Integration Live Transactions Infrastructure Deployment

Those aren’t the same category of evidence.
